summary: >-
  A pre-registered research design adjudicating among materialist, coalitional, and institutionally gated accounts of post-1990
  democratic erosion. The treatment is pre-fisc market inequality (WID pre-tax top-10 percent income share; market Gini secondary),
  measured against a pre-determined welfare gate of public health and education spending built in the first democratic decade,
  with the market-minus-disposable Gini gap directly measuring the automatic-stabilization leg. The gate is identified off
  welfare-specific trends with staggered event-study estimators built for differential timing; the cohort is capped at 1989-1998
  transitions so welfare precedes the 2008 crisis and the 2010-2022 resilience window; a fixed roster, coverage matrix, legacy-instrument
  2SLS, exogeneity probes, and a simulation-based minimum-detectable-effect analysis are deposited in a timestamped registry.
  Confirmation requires a significant pre-fisc-inequality-by-welfare interaction with the marginal-effect pattern in the primary
  specification and at least 5 of 7 robustness cells; disconfirmation adjudicates toward unconditional materialist or purely
  coalitional accounts. No models have been estimated: the paper is an honest pre-registration, and a null result is itself
  the contribution.
</paper_text>

   method figure when it has one.
4. RESULTS — the paper's real headline numbers, read out of `paper.tex` and the data

<writing_register>
Write in the register of the field's best papers (the paper this page presents, which was written to them), not in the register of a language
model. Four things are measured on the finished draft, and a draft outside them is sent back with
the numbers:
- Never use: delve, underscore, showcase, intricate, pivotal, realm, commendable, meticulous, tapestry, garner, multifaceted, it is worth noting, plays a crucial role, not only ... but also. These are 10 to 30 times more frequent in machine-written abstracts than in
  human ones, and reviewers read them as such.
- Em dashes: at most 3 per 1,000 words. Use a comma, a colon or a full stop.
- Sentence rhythm: mix short and long sentences. An interquartile range of sentence length under
  8 words reads as machine-written.
- Hedging: at most 15 hedges (may, likely, suggests, appears) per 1,000
  words. State what the evidence supports plainly; hedge where it is thin, not everywhere.
Style never changes substance: numbers, claims, citations and figure markers stay exactly as the
evidence gives them. The user's original request (delivered as a separate message) overrides all
of this wherever the two conflict.
</writing_register>

The coalitional account argues, from close case comparison, that economic grievances did not systematically separate post-1990 backsliders from survivors \\citep{HaggardKaufman2021}. This paper argues that the contradiction is unresolved for a structural reason: neither account tests the conditioning structure, and the statistical account's treatment is entangled with the very institution the gate hypothesis implicates. Disposable-income inequality is post-fisc, and fiscal systems that compress it are larger where welfare states are larger, so a gate estimated on the disposable Gini cannot separate institutional transmission from arithmetic filtering. We register a design that corrects both problems: the treatment is pre-fisc, the World Inequality Database pre-tax top-10 percent income share, with the market-income Gini secondary. The fiscal filter is measured directly as the market-minus-disposable Gini gap, converting the entanglement into the test of the stabilization mechanism. Among post-1990 democratizers whose transition began between 1989 and 1998, the hypothesis is that market-inequality surges erode the V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index three to five years later only where universal public health and education services built in the first democratic decade are thin. The gate is identified off deviations from welfare-specific trends, with estimators built for differential treatment timing, a fixed roster with a documented coverage matrix, and a simulation-based minimum-detectable-effect analysis. Confirmation and disconfirmation criteria are fixed ex ante, with a primary-specification significance rule and a five-of-seven robustness threshold. The design is built so the test can adjudicate between unconditional materialist, purely coalitional, and institutionally gated accounts.\n    31\t\\end{abstract}\n    32\t\n    33\t\\section{Introduction}\n    34\t\n    35\tSince the late twentieth century the main threat to democratic regimes has changed character. The military coup has given way to the power-aggrandizing elected executive: presidents and prime ministers who capture courts, harass the press, and de-legitimize elections \\citep{RauStokes2025, WaldnerLust2018, Bermeo2016, LevitskyZiblatt2018}. Erosion is now understood as a graded, incremental process inside formally democratic regimes, and a third wave of autocratization is dated to the late 2000s \\citep{LuhrmannLindberg2019}. The process descends from national executives to state governments \\citep{Grumbach2023}. The question that dominated twentieth-century comparative politics, what kills democracies, has been replaced by a harder one: how much democratic quality does a regime lose, and which democracies lose almost none?\n    36\t\n    37\tTwo answers compete. The materialist account points to income inequality. In a cross-national sample of democracies that remained uninterrupted over 1995--2020, Rau and Stokes count 23 spells of backsliding in 22 countries, lasting nine years on average, and find that the Gini coefficient is among the strongest predictors of erosion onset \\citep{RauStokes2025}. The result extends an older one: in the coup era, inequality harmed democratic consolidation even where it did not block democratization \\citep{Houle2009}, in line with the distributional-conflict tradition in which redistribution is the pivot of regime conflict \\citep{AcemogluRobinson2006, Boix2003, AnsellSamuels2014}. The coalitional account pushes back. **Contributions (4 cards):**
1. Reconciling the two accounts: the gate identifies the institutional condition under which each account holds: inequality erodes democracy where welfare institutions are thin; the coalitional story dominates where they are thick.
2. Fixing the treatment: the materialist account's flagship treatment, the disposable Gini, is compressed by the very fiscal systems the gate hypothesis implicates. The registered design moves the treatment pre-fisc (WID pre-tax top-10 percent share) and measures the fiscal filter directly as the market-minus-disposable Gini gap.
3. Conditioning the democratic dividend: states the dividend on top-income shares over a fixed post-transition window (years 0–7) and links its size to regime resilience in 2010–2022, conditioning the inequality leg on welfare institutions.
4. Identification and honest power: the gate is identified off deviations from welfare-specific trends with estimators for differential timing, exogeneity probes, a fixed roster with a coverage matrix, and a simulation-based MDES whose criteria match the power the sample can deliver.

**Method walkthrough:**
- Step 1 — The sample: post-1990 democratizers, transitions 1989–1998 (cohort cap so first democratic decade precedes the 2008 crisis and the 2010–2022 window), expected roster 25–35 countries, panel 1985–2023. Transition dated from V-Dem RoW cross-checked with Boix-Miller-Rosato.
- Step 2 — The treatment and the outcome: pre-fisc WID top-10 share lagged three years (distributed lags 1–6); secondary market Gini; disposable Gini demoted to robustness, used only to construct the gap g = m − d. Outcome: V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index (0–1), levels and five-year differences; erosion onset = three-year sustained decline ≥ 0.03.
- Step 3 — The gate: W = gov health spending %GDP + gov education spending %GDP, averaged over the earliest available three-year window in years 0–8 after transition, time-invariant thereafter. Why this measure: non-cash, middle-class-enrolled, automatic; excludes pensions and targeted cash by construction.
- Step 4 — The decomposition: dLibDem/dm = fiscal filtering + behavioral transmission. If gap control kills the interaction → stabilization is the whole mechanism; if it survives → constituency formation and pre-commitment do the work.
- Step 5 — Estimation: Design 1 with welfare-specific trends (the equation); five-year differences + Goodman-Bacon; Design 2 adjudication; Design 3 staggered event studies (Callaway-Sant'Anna, Sun-Abraham) for sequencing; Design 4 democratization event study for the dividend; Design 5 mechanism arms; Design 6 seven robustness cells. Exogeneity probes: balancing regressions, legacy-instrument 2SLS, within-Eastern-Europe, placebo moderator, early-erosion exclusion.
- Why the design is the way it is: the focal problem is that disposable inequality is entangled with welfare; everything else (pre-determined W, cohort cap, trends, registry) follows from making the pre-determined precede the outcome.

HERO:

Kicker: PRE-REGISTERED RESEARCH DESIGN — NO MODEL ESTIMATED
H1: The Welfare Gate: Pre-Fisc Inequality, Universal Public Services, and Democratic Resilience in Post-1990 Democratizers

TL;DR (plain language): 
"The democratic-erosion literature is split. One camp finds that income inequality is among the strongest predictors of democratic decline; the other finds, from close case comparison, that economic grievances did not separate post-1990 backsliders from survivors. This paper argues the dispute is unfalsifiable as both sides run it: the statistical camp tests no conditioning structure, and its headline treatment, the disposable-income Gini, is compressed by exactly the welfare state the gate hypothesis implicates. The paper registers the design that can decide: market-inequality surges, measured pre-fisc, erode liberal democracy three to five years later only where universal public health and education services built in the first democratic decade are thin. The number that frames the test: the gate holds only if the inequality-by-welfare interaction is significant at p < 0.05 in the primary specification and in at least five of the seven robustness cells. No model has been estimated; none exists yet. This page is the design."

That's ~150 words for the TL;DR. Good. Mention links below.

Links: "Read the paper (PDF)" and "Code and repository".

CONTRIBUTIONS (4 cards):

1. Reconciliation on institutional grounds.
"The gate is the condition under which each account holds: inequality erodes democracy where welfare institutions are thin, and the coalitional story dominates where they are thick. One design, not two literatures, now tests both."

2. A treatment the institutions cannot compress.
"The materialist account's flagship measure, disposable-income inequality, is post-fisc: fiscal systems that compress it are larger where welfare states are larger. The registered design moves the treatment pre-fisc (the WID pre-tax top-10 percent income share) and measures the fiscal filter directly as the market-minus-disposable Gini gap, converting the entanglement into the test of the stabilization mechanism."

3. The democratic dividend, conditioned.
"The paper states the dividend on top-income shares over a fixed post-transition window, years 0 to 7, and links its size to regime resilience in 2010-2022: democratization reduces top-end inequality only in high-welfare-legacy countries."

4. Identification and power stated before the results.
"The gate is identified off deviations from welfare-specific trends, with estimators built for differential treatment timing, a fixed roster with a documented coverage matrix, exogeneity probes, and a simulation-based minimum-detectable-effect analysis, so the confirmation criteria match the power the sample can actually deliver."

TL;DR text (final):

"The democratic-erosion literature is split. One camp finds that income inequality is among the strongest predictors of democratic decline in a global sample. The other, reading the same post-1990 wave as a set of cases, finds that economic grievances did not systematically separate backsliders from survivors. This paper argues the dispute is unfalsifiable as both sides run it: the statistical camp tests no conditioning structure, and its flagship treatment, disposable-income inequality, is compressed by exactly the welfare state the gate hypothesis implicates. The registered design fixes both problems. Market-inequality surges, measured pre-fisc, erode the V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index three to five years later only where universal public health and education services built in the first democratic decade are thin. The number that frames the test: the gate holds only if the inequality-by-welfare interaction is significant at p < 0.05 in the primary specification and in at least five of the seven robustness cells. No model has been estimated. The estimates do not exist yet; this page is the design."

METHOD sections:

Intro paragraph (the dispute paragraph):
"Two accounts of post-1990 democratic erosion face each other, and neither design can resolve the disagreement. Rau and Stokes estimate a main effect: the Gini coefficient is among the strongest predictors of erosion onset among uninterrupted democracies over 1995–2020, with 23 spells in 22 countries. Haggard and Kaufman compare backsliders with survivors and conclude that economic grievances did not do the separating. The statistical account contains no welfare variables, so it cannot see whether its inequality coefficient is carried by thin-welfare democracies. The case-based account never formalizes the interaction a conditional claim requires. Both miss the same object: the welfare state."

What goes in (h3):
- Sample paragraph: "The treated population is the post-1990 democratizers whose transitions began between 1989 and 1998, an expected roster of 25 to 35 countries over a 1985–2023 panel. The cohort cap is the identification. Every retained case's first democratic decade ends before the 2008 crisis and before the 2010–2022 resilience window, so the welfare measure always precedes the outcomes it explains. Transitions are dated from the V-Dem Regimes of the World series and cross-checked against Boix-Miller-Rosato; the roster is fixed before estimation and no case is added or dropped after."
- Treatment/outcome: "The primary treatment is the WID pre-tax national-income top-10 percent income share, lagged three years in the main specification with distributed lags tracing years one through six. Pre-tax by construction: Rau and Stokes use the same WID shares at the top end of their analysis, while their Gini is post-fisc, which is the entanglement. The market-income Gini is the secondary treatment; the disposable Gini is demoted to robustness and appears only to construct the gap. The outcome is the V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index, 0 to 1, in levels and in five-year differences, with erosion onset coded as the first year of a sustained three-year decline of at least 0.03."
- The gate: "The welfare gate W is the sum of government health and education spending, both percent of GDP, averaged over the earliest available three-year window within years 0 to 8 after transition and held time-invariant. It is deliberately non-cash: public health and public education are the components the broad middle class uses, the components automatic in delivery, and the components an eroding executive must capture. Pensions and targeted cash are excluded by construction; they are the placebo moderators of hypothesis H5."

The gate and its two paths (h3):
"The gate decomposes a market shock into two terms. The first is arithmetic. The fiscal filter g = m − d, the market-minus-disposable Gini gap, is the share of any market shock the fiscal system removes before the distribution reaches citizens; a design that treats disposable inequality as the treatment and welfare as a moderator conflates the two terms. The second is behavioral: the residue of the shock that reaches citizens, gated by constituency formation, by which the middle class holds a material stake in public institutions, and by credible pre-commitment, by which universal automatic programs block the populist-promise equilibrium. The gap is measured directly and entered as a covariate and as a moderator. If gap control drives the interaction to zero, automatic stabilization is the whole mechanism. If the interaction survives, constituency formation and pre-commitment get the credit, and Designs 5 and 6 are built to assign it."

"dLibDem/dm = ∂LibDem/∂d · (1 − φ(W)) [fiscal filtering] + ∂LibDem/∂m|d̄ [behavioral transmission]"

(the equation in a block)

What comes out (h3): Design 1 + the equation + readings:
"The core specification is a two-way fixed-effects regression with welfare-specific trends: [equation]. The interaction β₂ is the gate. The welfare-specific trends are the identification change this registration makes: any factor correlated with welfare strength and with democratic trajectories, EU accession, fiscal capacity, geopolitical alignment, is absorbed, and the gate is identified off deviations from welfare-specific trends. The hypothesis is β₂ > 0, with the marginal effect reported at the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentiles of the welfare distribution: near zero or positive in the high-welfare arm, strongly negative in the thin-welfare arm."

The six designs (h3) — a dl or ol:
1. Design 1, the gate test. Two-way fixed effects with welfare-specific trends; the gap-controlled variant whose reading is fixed in advance.
2. Design 2, the adjudication. The inequality main effect with and without the interaction, on the full and the young-democracy samples. Weak main effect plus strong interaction reconciles the accounts; a surviving unconditional effect favors the materialist account; a null everywhere favors the coalitional account.
3. Design 3, sequencing. Erosion-onset event studies with Callaway-Sant'Anna and Sun-Abraham estimators, separately by welfare arm; lead-lag tests distinguish the gate from reverse causation.
4. Design 4, the dividend. A democratization event study aligned at transition; the top-10 percent share, services and education over two decades, by welfare legacy; the dividend window is years 0 to 7, and its size predicts the 2010–2022 change in liberal democracy.
5. Design 5, mechanisms. Four arms: gap control for stabilization, composition and usage controls for constituency formation, the automaticity index for pre-commitment, and a proximate-channel report on polarization and educated-youth unemployment.
6. Design 6, robustness. Seven pre-committed cells, every one reported including the failures: alternative treatments, alternative welfare measures, population weights, commodity-boom exclusion, within-Eastern-Europe estimates and the early-erosion exclusion, wild cluster bootstrap inference, and the placebo moderators.

Then "Why the design is shaped this way" (h3):
"The whole design hangs on one logical move: pre-determination must precede outcome. Welfare built in the first democratic decade, before crises arrive, gates the inequality-erosion link; welfare generosity purchased later by incumbents is not a substitute, it is part of the erosion playbook. Five exogeneity probes confront the threat that the first democratic decade itself selects welfare depth: balancing regressions of W on first-decade inequality and fiscal collapse; legacy-instrument 2SLS using communist-era schooling and colonial-era service coverage; the within-Eastern-Europe estimate; the placebo moderator; and the early-erosion exclusion. The power analysis is honest about the sample: minimum detectable effects are simulated on the realized panel at 80 percent power under serial correlation of 0.7, 0.8 and 0.9 and effective N of 25, 30 and 35, and the confirmation criteria are calibrated to detect a large conditional effect only. A weak gate will go undetected, and the results paper will say so."

The five hypotheses (h3) — compact list:
H1 (the gate). Effect is negative and large in thin-welfare countries, near zero or positive where welfare is strong; interaction positive under welfare-specific trends.
H2 (sequencing). Surges and retrenchment lead declines by three to five years in thin-welfare countries; no anticipatory service decline in high-welfare countries.
H3 (the welfare-dependent dividend). Top-10 percent share declines in years 0 to 7 only in high-welfare-legacy countries; the decline predicts 2010–2022 resilience.
H4 (mechanisms). At least one of: gap control kills the interaction (stabilization); composition and usage controls attenuate it (constituency formation); automatic programs gate and discretionary transfers do not (pre-commitment); or the interaction operates through polarization and education-without-absorption.
H5 (universalism contrast). Public services gate; total social spending and late-bought transfers are placebo moderators that do not gate.

B. "The trajectories the design must explain" — table (as above). Caption: "Liberal Democracy Index and welfare sums, from Section 4.7. Values from the development phase, to be re-verified at every series URL in the coverage audit."

Include the inequality-levels paragraph: "The eroded countries were not the most unequal. Hungary's disposable Gini ran between 0.27 and 0.35 over 2005–2016 with a trough of 0.270 in 2009; Poland's fell from 0.38 in 2004 to 0.31 in 2016. The resilient countries were not the most equal: Estonia's Gini held between 0.31 and 0.35, Latvia's between 0.34 and 0.39. The level correlation is weak in exactly the way Haggard and Kaufman describe, which is why the theory is stated in shocks, not levels: the gate conditions the transmission of inequality increases."

C. "Decision rules fixed ex ante" — table (as above). Caption: "From Sections 5 and 6 of the paper. Every rule is fixed and deposited before estimation; no specification is added or dropped after."

LIMITATIONS: intro line: "Five limitations are intrinsic to the design, and the paper states them as such rather than as future work (Section 8)."
1. Small N and statistical power. 25–35 countries; the interaction is a difference-in-differences of a difference-in-differences; power is low; MDES defines what can be detected; a weak gate will go undetected and the results paper will say so if the confidence intervals cannot exclude one.
2. The welfare measure is a proxy. Spending as a share of GDP measures fiscal effort, not universality, quality or use by the middle class; the bias is conservative, attenuating the interaction and biasing against confirmation.
3. Identification of the gate. W is pre-determined but not randomly assigned; first-decade governments that consolidated well also maintained services; the probes and trends address specific versions of the threat but none eliminates a third factor driving both welfare maintenance and democratic resilience; EU accession is partially entangled by construction.
4. Measurement of the outcome and the treatment. The Liberal Democracy Index is expert-coded and its inter-temporal comparability is contested; Gini comparability is limited by surveys and income concepts; a misdated onset could shift the sequencing tests, addressed by the coding rule and the requirement that the pattern differ across welfare arms.
5. The placebo subsample problem. The OECD SOCX measure exists only for OECD members, so H5's sharpest contrast relies on the full-sample transfer measure; if that series is unavailable on OWID for a substantial share of the roster, the finding is itself a registered limitation.

FOOTER: "The Welfare Gate: Pre-Fisc Inequality, Universal Public Services, and Democratic Resilience in Post-1990 Democratizers. A pre-registered research design. Protocol, country roster, coverage matrix, minimum-detectable-effect analysis and code are deposited in a timestamped OSF registry before estimation; registration ID and deposit date are fixed at the moment of deposit. No model has been estimated; a companion paper will report estimates against the criteria fixed here." + links.

"The democratic-erosion literature is split. One camp finds that income inequality is among the strongest predictors of democratic decline in a global sample of uninterrupted democracies. The other, reading the post-1990 wave case by case, finds that economic grievances did not systematically separate backsliders from survivors. This paper argues the dispute is unfalsifiable as both sides run it: the statistical camp tests no conditioning structure, and its flagship treatment, disposable-income inequality, is post-fisc, compressed by exactly the welfare state the gate hypothesis implicates. The registered design corrects both problems. Market-inequality surges, measured pre-fisc, erode the V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index three to five years later only where universal public health and education services built in the first democratic decade are thin. The number that frames the test: the gate holds only if the inequality-by-welfare interaction is significant at p < 0.05 in the primary specification and in at least five of the seven robustness cells. No model has been estimated. The estimates do not exist yet; this page is the design."

"Rau and Stokes estimate a main effect: in a sample of democracies uninterrupted over 1995-2020, the Gini coefficient is among the strongest predictors of erosion onset, with 23 spells of backsliding in 22 countries. Haggard and Kaufman compare backsliders with survivors and conclude that economic grievances did not do the separating; polarization and elite coalitional choices did. The statistical account contains no welfare variables, so it cannot see whether its inequality coefficient is carried by thin-welfare democracies. The case-based account never formalizes the interaction a conditional claim requires. Both miss the same object, and the field's flagship treatment is entangled with it: disposable income is post-fisc, and the fiscal systems that compress it are the welfare states this hypothesis implicates."

"Building blocks" h3 — "What goes in":
Four items (dl or ul):
- Sample: "Post-1990 democratizers with transitions beginning 1989-1998, expected roster of 25 to 35 countries, panel 1985-2023. The cohort cap makes pre-determination possible: every retained case's first democratic decade ends before the 2008 crisis and before the 2010-2022 resilience window. Transition is dated from the V-Dem Regimes of the World series and cross-checked against Boix-Miller-Rosato; the roster is fixed deterministically and no case is added or dropped after estimation begins."
- Treatment: "The primary treatment is the WID pre-tax national-income top-10 percent income share, the measure type Rau and Stokes themselves use at the top end of their analysis. It is lagged three years in the main specification, with distributed lags tracing years one through six, implementing the three-to-five-year transmission window. The market-income Gini is the secondary treatment. The disposable Gini, where the entanglement lives, is demoted to robustness and enters only to construct the gap."
- Gate: "The welfare gate W is the sum of government health expenditure and government education expenditure, both as a share of GDP, averaged over the earliest available three-year window within years 0 to 8 after transition and held time-invariant. It is deliberately non-cash: health and education are what the broad middle class uses, what is automatic in delivery, and what an eroding executive must capture. Pensions and targeted cash are excluded by construction, and they become the placebo moderators of H5."
- Outcome: "The V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index, 0 to 1, in levels and five-year differences. A continuous index is essential: the hypothesis concerns graded erosion inside formally democratic regimes. Erosion onset is coded as the first year of a sustained three-year decline of at least 0.03."

"The gate and its two paths" h3:
"The total effect of a market shock on liberal-democratic quality decomposes into two terms. The first is arithmetic: [equation]. The fiscal filter, the market-minus-disposable Gini gap, is the share of any market shock the fiscal system removes before the distribution reaches citizens; it operates even if no citizen changes behavior. The second is behavioral: the residue of the shock that reaches citizens, gated by constituency formation, by which a middle class that uses public services holds a material stake in the institutions erosion would capture, and by credible pre-commitment, by which universal automatic programs block the populist-promise equilibrium. The design measures the gap directly and enters it as a covariate and as a moderator. If gap control drives the interaction to zero, automatic stabilization is the entire mechanism. If the interaction survives, a behavioral residue exists and Designs 5 and 6 exist to attribute it."

"Estimating the gate" h3:
"The core specification is Design 1, a two-way fixed-effects regression with welfare-specific trends: [equation block]. The interaction coefficient β₂ is the gate: hypothesis H1 is β₂ > 0, with the marginal effect near zero or positive in the high-welfare arm and strongly negative in the thin-welfare arm. The welfare-specific trends are the identification change this registration makes. Any factor correlated with welfare strength and with democratic trajectories, EU accession, fiscal capacity, geopolitical alignment, is absorbed in the trend terms, and the gate is identified off deviations from welfare-specific trends. Because two-way fixed effects with differential timing can be biased under heterogeneous effects, the interacted specification is also estimated on five-year differences of the outcome, with Goodman-Bacon decompositions, Callaway-Sant'Anna and Sun-Abraham estimators in the event studies, and wild cluster bootstrap inference for the interaction test."

"The six designs" h3 — ordered list (ol) with strong lead-ins, one or two sentences each:
1. Design 1, the gate test. "The two-way fixed-effects specification with welfare-specific trends, plus the pre-committed gap-controlled variant whose reading is fixed in advance."
2. Design 2, the adjudication. "The inequality main effect with and without the interaction, on the full democracy sample and on the young-democracy sample. A weak main effect with a strong interaction reconciles the two accounts. A surviving unconditional effect favors the materialist account; a null everywhere favors the coalitional account."
3. Design 3, sequencing. "Erosion-onset event studies estimated separately in the high-welfare and thin-welfare arms, with pre-trend tests. The lead-lag structure is the primary defense against reverse causality: services must fall before the index in the thin-welfare arm and not at all in the high-welfare arm."
4. Design 4, the dividend. "A democratization event study aligned at transition, tracing the top-10 percent share, services and education over two decades by welfare legacy. The dividend window is fixed at years 0 to 7, so it precedes the 2008 crisis and the 2010-2022 resilience window for every retained case."
5. Design 5, mechanisms. "Four arms: gap control for stabilization; composition and usage controls for constituency formation; the automaticity index for pre-commitment; a proximate-channel report on polarization and educated-youth unemployment."
6. Design 6, robustness. "Seven pre-committed cells, every one reported including the failures: alternative treatments, alternative welfare measures, population weights, commodity-boom exclusion, within-Eastern-Europe estimates and the early-erosion exclusion, wild cluster bootstrap inference, and the placebo moderators."

"Why the design is shaped this way" h3:
"Everything hangs on one logical move: the pre-determined must precede the outcome it explains. Welfare institutions built in the first democratic decade, before crises arrive, gate the inequality-erosion link; welfare generosity purchased later by incumbents is not a substitute, it is part of the erosion playbook. Five exogeneity probes confront the threat that the first democratic decade itself selects welfare depth: balancing regressions of W on first-decade inequality changes and fiscal collapse; legacy-instrument 2SLS using communist-era schooling enrollment and colonial-era public-service coverage; the within-Eastern-Europe estimate, which holds the communist legacy constant; the placebo moderator, which predicts that a pension-heavy total-spending measure does not gate; and the early-erosion exclusion. The power analysis is calibrated to the same honesty. Minimum detectable effects are simulated on the realized panel at 80 percent power, under outcome serial correlation of 0.7, 0.8 and 0.9 and effective N of 25, 30 and 35. The study is powered to detect a large conditional effect, which is what the theory predicts; a weak gate will go undetected, and the results paper will say so rather than claim a null."

"The five hypotheses" h3 — definition list:
H1 The gate. "The within-country effect of a lagged market-inequality increase on the Liberal Democracy Index is negative and large in thin-welfare countries and near zero or positive in strong-welfare countries; the interaction is positive and significant under welfare-specific trend controls."
H2 Sequencing. "Market-inequality surges and public-services retrenchment lead liberal-democracy declines by three to five years in thin-welfare countries, with no anticipatory service decline before erosion onset in high-welfare countries."
H3 The welfare-dependent dividend. "Democratization reduces the top-10 percent income share in the first post-transition years only in high-welfare-legacy countries, and the size of that first-decade decline predicts 2010-2022 resilience."
H4 Mechanisms. "At least one discriminating result: gap control kills the interaction (stabilization); composition and usage controls attenuate it (constituency formation); automatic programs gate and discretionary transfers do not (pre-commitment); or the interaction runs through polarization and tightens where education expands without absorption."
H5 The universalism contrast. "Public health and education services gate; total social spending, pension-heavy and transfer-dominated, and late-bought targeted or chauvinist transfers are placebo moderators that do not gate."

max-width: 46rem; }\n  footer .cite .title { font-style: italic; color: var(--ink-mid); }\n  footer .f-links { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1.4rem; margin: 1.1rem 0 0; }\n  footer a { color: var(--accent-deep); }\n  footer .status { max-width: 46rem; margin-top: 1.1rem; }\n\n  /* ---- Tablet / desktop ---- */\n  @media (min-width: 900px) {\n    .cards { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }\n  }\n  @media (min-width: 1024px) {\n    .layout { grid-template-columns: 13.5rem minmax(0, 1fr); column-gap: 3.25rem; }\n    .side-nav {\n      position: sticky;\n      top: 2.4rem;\n      align-self: start;\n      background: none;\n      border-bottom: 0;\n      margin: 0;\n      padding: 0.6rem 0 0;\n      overflow: visible;\n    }\n    .side-nav ul { flex-direction: column; gap: 0.12rem; white-space: normal; padding: 0; border-left: 1px solid var(--hairline); }\n    .side-nav li { margin: 0; }\n    .side-nav a {\n      display: block;\n      padding: 0.42rem 0.95rem;\n      border-bottom: 0;\n      border-left: 2px solid transparent;\n      margin-left: -1px;\n      font-size: 0.86rem;\n      letter-spacing: 0.02em;\n      text-transform: none;\n      font-weight: 570;\n    }\n    .side-nav a[aria-current=\"true\"] { border-bottom: 0; border-left-color: var(--accent); }\n    section { scroll-margin-top: 1.5rem; }\n  }\n\n  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\n    *, *::before, *::after {\n      animation: none !important;\n      transition: none !important;\n      scroll-behavior: auto !important;\n    }\n  }\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n<a class=\"skip-link\" href=\"#main\">Skip to main content</a>\n\n<div class=\"shell\">\n  <div class=\"layout\">\n\n    <nav class=\"side-nav\" id=\"section-nav\" aria-label=\"Page sections\">\n      <ul>\n        <li><a href=\"#overview\">Overview</a></li>\n        <li><a href=\"#contributions\">Contributions</a></li>\n        <li><a href=\"#method\">Method</a></li>\n        <li><a href=\"#results\">Results</a></li>\n        <li><a href=\"#limitations\">Limitations</a></li>\n      </ul>\n    </nav>\n\n    <div class=\"content\">\n\n      <header class=\"hero\" id=\"overview\">\n        <p class=\"kicker\">Pre-registered research design &middot; no model estimated</p>\n        <h1>The Welfare Gate: Pre-Fisc Inequality, Universal Public Services, and Democratic Resilience in Post-1990 Democratizers</h1>\n        <p class=\"lede\">\n          The democratic-erosion literature is split. One camp finds that income inequality is among the strongest\n          predictors of democratic decline in a global sample of uninterrupted democracies [1]. The other, reading the\n          post-1990 wave case by case, finds that economic grievances did not systematically separate backsliders from\n          survivors [2]. This paper argues the dispute is unfalsifiable as both sides run it: the statistical camp\n          tests no conditioning structure, and its flagship treatment, disposable-income inequality, is post-fisc,\n          compressed by exactly the welfare state the gate hypothesis implicates. The registered design corrects both\n          problems. Market-inequality surges, measured pre-fisc, erode the V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index\n          <span class=\"num\">three to five years</span> later only where universal public health and education services\n          built in the first democratic decade are thin. The number that frames the test: the gate holds only if the\n          inequality-by-welfare interaction is significant at <i>p</i>&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;0.05 in the primary specification\n          and in <span class=\"num\">at least five of the seven</span> robustness cells. No model has been estimated.\n          The estimates do not exist yet; this page is the design.\n        </p>\n        <div class=\"hero-links\">\n          <a class=\"btn primary\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-77624d-the-welfare-gate-pre-fisc-inequality@main/paper.pdf\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n          <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-77624d-the-welfare-gate-pre-fisc-inequality\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\">Code and repository</a>\n        </div>\n      </header>\n\n      <main id=\"main\">\n\n        <section id=\"contributions\" aria-labelledby=\"contributions-h\">\n          <h2 id=\"contributions-h\"><span class=\"idx\">01</span>Contributions</h2>\n          <p class=\"lead\">Four claims, each registered before any estimation.</p>\n          <div class=\"cards\">\n            <div class=\"card\">\n              <h3>Reconciliation on institutional grounds</h3>\n              <p>Neither leading account tests the conditioning structure. This design identifies the condition under\n              which each holds: inequality erodes democracy where welfare institutions are thin, and the coalitional\n              story dominates where they are thick. One interaction test, not two literatures, adjudicates the dispute.</p>\n            </div>\n            <div class=\"card\">\n              <h3>A treatment the institutions cannot compress</h3>\n              <p>Disposable-income inequality is post-fisc, and fiscal systems that compress it are larger where welfare\n              states are larger, so a gate estimated on the disposable Gini cannot separate institutional transmission\n              from arithmetic filtering. The treatment moves pre-fisc, to the WID pre-tax top-10 percent income share,\n              and the market-minus-disposable Gini gap is measured directly, turning the entanglement into a test of\n              the stabilization mechanism.</p>\n            </div>\n            <div class=\"card\">\n              <h3>The democratic dividend, conditioned</h3>\n              <p>Democratization raises tax revenues and schooling but shows no robust average effect on inequality.\n              The design states the dividend on top-income shares over a fixed post-transition window, years 0 to 7,\n              and links its size to regime resilience in 2010&ndash;2022: the inequality-reduction leg materializes\n              only in high-welfare-legacy countries.</p>\n            </div>\n            <div class=\"card\">\n              <h3>Identification and power fixed before the results</h3>\n              <p>The gate is identified off deviations from welfare-specific trends, with estimators built for\n              differential treatment timing, a fixed roster with a documented coverage matrix, exogeneity probes, and\n              a simulation-based minimum-detectable-effect analysis. The confirmation criteria are calibrated to the\n              power the sample can actually deliver.</p>\n            </div>\n          </div>\n        </section>\n\n        <section id=\"method\" aria-labelledby=\"method-h\">\n          <h2 id=\"method-h\"><span class=\"idx\">02</span>Method</h2>\n\n          <h3>The dispute neither side can resolve</h3>\n          <p>Rau and Stokes estimate a main effect: in a sample of democracies uninterrupted over 1995&ndash;2020, the\n          Gini coefficient is among the strongest predictors of erosion onset, with <span class=\"num\">23 spells of\n          backsliding in 22 countries</span>. Haggard and Kaufman compare backsliders with survivors and conclude that\n          economic grievances did not do the separating; polarization and elite coalitional choices did. The\n          statistical account contains no welfare variables, so it cannot see whether its inequality coefficient is\n          carried by thin-welfare democracies. The case-based account never formalizes the interaction a conditional\n          claim requires. Both miss the same object, and the field's flagship treatment is entangled with it:\n          disposable income is post-fisc, and the fiscal systems that compress it are the welfare states this\n          hypothesis implicates.</p>\n\n          <h3>What goes in</h3>\n          <ul class=\"blocks\">\n            <li><strong>Sample.</strong> Post-1990 democratizers with transitions beginning 1989&ndash;1998, an\n            expected roster of <span class=\"num\">25 to 35 countries</span> over a panel running 1985&ndash;2023. The\n            cohort cap makes pre-determination possible: every retained case's first democratic decade ends before the\n            2008 crisis and before the 2010&ndash;2022 resilience window. Transition is dated from the V-Dem Regimes\n            of the World series and cross-checked against Boix&ndash;Miller&ndash;Rosato; the roster is fixed\n            deterministically, and no case is added or dropped after estimation begins.</li>\n            <li><strong>Treatment.</strong> The primary treatment is the Warld-free World Inequality Database\n            pre-tax national-income top-10 percent income share, the measure type Rau and Stokes use at the top end of\n            their own analysis. It is lagged three years in the main specification, with distributed lags tracing\n            years one through six, implementing the three-to-five-year transmission window. The market-income Gini is\n            the secondary treatment; the disposable Gini, where the entanglement lives, enters only to construct the\n            gap.</li>\n            <li><strong>Gate.</strong> The welfare variable <i>W</i> is the sum of government health expenditure and\n            government education expenditure, both as a share of GDP, averaged over the earliest available three-year\n            window within years 0 to 8 after transition and held time-invariant. It is deliberately non-cash: health\n            and education are what the broad middle class uses, what is automatic in delivery, and what an eroding\n            executive must capture. Pensions and targeted cash are excluded by construction, and they become the\n            placebo moderators of H5.</li>\n            <li><strong>Outcome.</strong> The V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index, 0 to 1, in levels and in five-year\n            differences. A continuous index is essential: the hypothesis concerns graded erosion inside formally\n            democratic regimes. Erosion onset is coded as the first year of a sustained three-year decline of at\n            least <span class=\"num\">0.03</span>.</li>\n          </ul>\n\n          <h3>The gate and its two paths</h3>\n          <p>A market shock reaches liberal-democratic quality through two terms, and the design measures them\n          separately. The first is arithmetic: the market-minus-disposable Gini gap absorbs part of any shock before\n          the distribution reaches citizens, and this works even if no citizen changes behavior. The second is\n          behavioral: the residue of the shock that does reach citizens, gated by constituency formation, by which a\n          middle class that uses public services holds a material stake in the institutions erosion would capture,\n          and by credible pre-commitment, by which universal automatic programs block the populist-promise\n          equilibrium.</p>\n          <div class=\"eq\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n            <span class=\"term\">d&#8201;LibDem / d&#8201;m = [ &part;LibDem/&part;d &middot; (1 &minus; &phi;(W)) ]\n            <span class=\"lbl\">fiscal filtering</span></span>\n            <span class=\"op\">+</span>\n            <span class=\"term\">[ &part;LibDem/&part;m | d&#772; ]\n            <span class=\"lbl\">behavioral transmission</span></span>\n          </div>\n          <p>A design that treats disposable inequality as the treatment and welfare as the moderator conflates the\n          two terms. This design treats the pre-fisc shock as the treatment and enters the gap directly, as a\n          covariate and as a moderator. If gap control drives the interaction to zero, automatic stabilization is the\n          entire mechanism. If the interaction survives, a behavioral residue exists, and Designs 5 and 6 exist to\n          attribute it.</p>\n\n          <h3>Estimating the gate</h3>\n          <p>The core specification, Design 1, is a two-way fixed-effects regression with welfare-specific trends:</p>\n          <div class=\"eq\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n            LibDem<sub>it</sub> = &alpha;<sub>i</sub> + &delta;<sub>t</sub> + &beta;<sub>1</sub>&#8201;m<sub>i,t&minus;3</sub>\n            + &beta;<sub>2</sub>(m<sub>i,t&minus;3</sub> &times; W<sub>i</sub>)\n            + &gamma;<sub>1</sub>W<sub>i</sub>t + &gamma;<sub>2</sub>W<sub>i</sub>t<sup>2</sup>\n            + X&prime;<sub>it</sub>&theta; + &epsilon;<sub>it</sub>\n          </div>\n          <p>The interaction coefficient &beta;<sub>2</sub> is the gate. Hypothesis H1 is &beta;<sub>2</sub> &gt; 0,\n          with the marginal effect near zero or positive in the high-welfare arm and strongly negative in the\n          thin-welfare arm, reported at the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentiles of the welfare distribution.\n          The welfare-specific trends are the identification change this registration makes: any factor correlated\n          with welfare strength and with democratic trajectories, EU accession, fiscal capacity, geopolitical\n          alignment, is absorbed in the trend terms, and the gate is identified off deviations from welfare-specific\n          trends. Because two-way fixed effects with differential timing can be biased under heterogeneous effects,\n          the interacted specification is also estimated on five-year differences of the outcome, with\n          Goodman&ndash;Bacon decompositions, Callaway&ndash;Sant'Anna and Sun&ndash;Abraham estimators in the event\n          studies, and wild cluster bootstrap inference for the interaction test.</p>\n\n          <h3>The six designs</h3>\n          <ol class=\"designs\">\n            <li><strong>Design 1, the gate test.</strong> The two-way fixed-effects specification with welfare-specific\n            trends, plus the gap-controlled variant whose reading is fixed in advance.</li>\n            <li><strong>Design 2, the adjudication.</strong> The inequality main effect with and without the\n            interaction, on the full democracy sample and on the young-democracy sample. A weak main effect with a\n            strong interaction reconciles the two accounts. A surviving unconditional effect favors the materialist\n            account; a null everywhere favors the coalitional account.</li>\n            <li><strong>Design 3, sequencing.</strong> Erosion-onset event studies estimated separately in the\n            high-welfare and thin-welfare arms, with pre-trend tests. The lead-lag structure is the primary defense\n            against reverse causality: services must fall before the index in the thin-welfare arm, and not at all in\n            the high-welfare arm.</li>\n            <li><strong>Design 4, the dividend.</strong> A democratization event study aligned at transition, tracing\n            the top-10 percent share, services and education over two decades by welfare legacy. The dividend window\n            is fixed at years 0 to 7, so it precedes the 2008 crisis and the 2010&ndash;2022 resilience window for\n            every retained case.</li>\n            <li><strong>Design 5, mechanisms.</strong> Four arms: gap control for stabilization; composition and\n            usage controls for constituency formation; the automaticity index for pre-commitment; and a\n            proximate-channel report on polarization and educated-youth unemployment.</li>\n            <li><strong>Design 6, robustness.</strong> Seven pre-committed cells, every one reported including the\n            failures: alternative treatments, alternative welfare measures, population weights, commodity-boom\n            exclusion, within-Eastern-Europe estimates and the early-erosion exclusion, wild cluster bootstrap\n            inference, and the placebo moderators.</li>\n          </ol>\n\n          <h3>Why the design is shaped this way</h3>\n          <p>Everything hangs on one logical move: the pre-determined must precede the outcome it explains. Welfare\n          institutions built in the first democratic decade, before crises arrive, gate the inequality-erosion link;\n          welfare generosity purchased later by incumbents is not a substitute, it is part of the erosion playbook.\n          Five exogeneity probes confront the threat that the first democratic decade itself selects welfare depth:\n          balancing regressions of <i>W</i> on first-decade inequality changes and fiscal collapse; legacy-instrument\n          2SLS using communist-era schooling enrollment and colonial-era public-service coverage; the\n          within-Eastern-Europe estimate, which holds the communist legacy constant; the placebo moderator, which\n          predicts that a pension-heavy total-spending measure does not gate; and the early-erosion exclusion, which\n          removes cases for which <i>W</i> is post-treatment by construction.</p>\n          <p>The power analysis is calibrated to the same honesty. Minimum detectable effects are simulated on the\n          realized panel at <span class=\"num\">80 percent power</span>, under outcome serial correlation of 0.7, 0.8\n          and 0.9 and effective N of 25, 30 and 35. The study is powered to detect a large conditional effect, which\n          is what the theory predicts. A weak gate will go undetected, and the results paper will say so rather than\n          claim a null.</p>\n\n          <h3>The five hypotheses</h3>\n          <dl class=\"hyps\">\n            <dt><span class=\"hno\">H1</span> &middot; The gate</dt>\n            <dd>The within-country effect of a lagged market-inequality increase on the Liberal Democracy Index is\n            negative and large in thin-welfare countries and near zero or positive in strong-welfare countries; the\n            interaction is positive and significant under welfare-specific trend controls.</dd>\n            <dt><span class=\"hno\">H2</span> &middot; Sequencing</dt>\n            <dd>Market-inequality surges and public-services retrenchment lead liberal-democracy declines by three to\n            five years in thin-welfare countries, with no anticipatory service decline before erosion onset in\n            high-welfare countries.</dd>\n            <dt><span class=\"hno\">H3</span> &middot; The welfare-dependent dividend</dt>\n            <dd>Democratization reduces the top-10 percent income share in the first post-transition years only in\n            high-welfare-legacy countries, and the size of that first-decade decline predicts 2010&ndash;2022\n            resilience.</dd>\n            <dt><span class=\"hno\">H4</span> &middot; Mechanisms</dt>\n            <dd>At least one discriminating result: gap control kills the interaction (stabilization); composition and\n            usage controls attenuate it (constituency formation); automatic programs gate and discretionary transfers\n            do not (pre-commitment); or the interaction runs through polarization and tightens where education\n            expands without absorption.</dd>\n            <dt><span class=\"hno\">H5</span> &middot; The universalism contrast</dt>\n            <dd>Public health and education services gate; total social spending, pension-heavy and\n            transfer-dominated, and late-bought targeted or chauvinist transfers are placebo moderators that do not\n            gate.</dd>\n          </dl>\n        </section>\n\n        <section id=\"results\" aria-labelledby=\"results-h\">\n          <h2 id=\"results-h\"><span class=\"idx\">03</span>Results</h2>\n          <p class=\"lead\">The paper reports no estimates; none exist yet. What follows are the numbers the design is\n          built around, each as it appears in the paper: the calibration that frames the dispute, the trajectories\n          the design must explain, and the decision rules fixed before estimation.</p>\n\n          <h3>The calibration that frames the dispute</h3>\n          <p>Rau and Stokes calibrate their leading predictor against predicted annual erosion risk. Their sample:\n          23 spells of backsliding in 22 countries over 1995&ndash;2020, nine years on average, with main analyses\n          covering <span class=\"num\">92 countries</span>.</p>\n          <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n            <table>\n              <caption>Predicted annual risk of erosion onset by country, from Rau and Stokes 2025, as reported in\n              Section 2.1 of the paper.</caption>\n              <thead>\n                <tr>\n                  <th scope=\"col\">Country</th>\n                  <th scope=\"col\">Measured on</th>\n                  <th scope=\"col\" class=\"n\">Predicted annual risk</th>\n                  <th scope=\"col\">Compared with</th>\n                </tr>\n              </thead>\n              <tbody>\n                <tr>\n                  <td>Sweden</td>\n                  <td>Gini of 26.4 in 2017</td>\n                  <td class=\"n\">4 percent</td>\n                  <td>more equal than 87 percent of democracies</td>\n                </tr>\n                <tr>\n                  <td>United States</td>\n                  <td>Gini of 38.4</td>\n                  <td class=\"n\">8.4 percent</td>\n                  <td>exceeds 60 percent of democracies</td>\n                </tr>\n                <tr>\n                  <td>South Africa</td>\n                  <td>most unequal democracy in the sample</td>\n                  <td class=\"n\">31 percent</td>\n                  <td>&mdash;</td>\n                </tr>\n              </tbody>\n            </table>\n          </div>\n          <p>The democratic-dividend literature supplies the second calibration: democratization raises the tax-to-GDP\n          ratio by about <span class=\"num\">16 percent</span> in the long run in the preferred specification, with no\n          robust average effect on inequality. The null is the field fact the gate explains.</p>\n\n          <h3>The trajectories the design must explain</h3>\n          <p>Among the eleven cases with continuous data, liberal-democratic quality diverged sharply after 2010.\n          The same wave produced both the sharpest erosion and the most stable resilience in the same region. Welfare\n          sums are the development-phase measure of <i>W</i>, health plus education spending as a share of GDP.</p>\n          <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n            <table>\n              <caption>Liberal Democracy Index (0&ndash;1) and welfare sums by country, from Section 4.7 of the\n              paper. Values from the development phase, to be re-verified at every series URL in the coverage audit.</caption>\n              <thead>\n                <tr>\n                  <th scope=\"col\">Country</th>\n                  <th scope=\"col\">Liberal Democracy Index</th>\n                  <th scope=\"col\" class=\"n\">Welfare sum, % of GDP</th>\n                </tr>\n              </thead>\n              <tbody>\n                <tr><td>Hungary</td><td>0.754 in 2005 &rarr; 0.335 in 2022</td><td class=\"n\">9.6</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Poland</td><td>0.827 in 2010 &rarr; 0.417 in 2022</td><td class=\"n\">8.9</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Estonia</td><td>0.811 &rarr; 0.853, 2010&ndash;2022</td><td class=\"n\">9.5</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Slovakia</td><td>held its 2005 level</td><td class=\"n\">9.0</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Latvia</td><td>held its 2005 level</td><td class=\"n\">8.4</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Lithuania</td><td>held its 2005 level</td><td class=\"n\">10.3</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Chile</td><td>consolidated after 2000, declined mildly after 2015</td><td class=\"n\">7.5</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>South Korea</td><td>fell mid-decade, recovered, ended 2022 at 0.718</td><td class=\"n\">5.1</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>South Africa</td><td>0.666 in 2010 &rarr; 0.610 in 2022</td><td class=\"n\">7.2</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Bulgaria, Romania</td><td>fluctuated in an intermediate band; no usable WHO health series in the early window on OWID</td><td class=\"n\">&mdash;</td></tr>\n              </tbody>\n            </table>\n          </div>\n          <p>The inequality levels do not line up with the erosion outcomes. Hungary's disposable Gini ran between\n          0.27 and 0.35 over 2005&ndash;2016, with a trough of 0.270 in 2009; Poland's fell from 0.38 in 2004 to 0.31\n          in 2016. The resilient countries were not the most equal: Estonia's Gini held between 0.31 and 0.35,\n          Latvia's between 0.34 and 0.39. The level correlation is weak in exactly the way Haggard and Kaufman\n          describe, which is why the theory is stated in shocks rather than levels: the gate conditions the\n          transmission of inequality increases, not the standing level of inequality.</p>\n          <p>South Africa is the sharpest case: the cohort's highest inequality, a Gini near 0.65 at its 2005 peak\n          and still 0.61 in 2010, with only modest liberal-democratic decline, from 0.666 in 2010 to 0.610 in 2022.\n          The paper reads the pattern as delayed or partial transmission, and the Design 3 timing tests are what\n          distinguish that reading from a materialist one.</p>\n\n          <h3>Decision rules fixed ex ante</h3>\n          <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n            <table>\n              <caption>Rules from Sections 5 and 6 of the paper. 0.05, with the marginal effect negative and excluding zero at the 10th and 25th percentiles of <i>W</i> and not significantly negative at the 90th percentile</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Robustness rule</td><td>Pattern confirmed in the primary specification and in at least five of the seven robustness cells; failures reported and interpreted</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Transmission window</td><td>Surges lead declines by three to five years; treatment lagged three years, distributed lags tracing years one through six</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Power</td><td>Simulation-based MDES at 80 percent power, outcome serial correlation 0.7, 0.8 and 0.9, effective N 25, 30 and 35</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Cohort and roster</td><td>Transitions beginning 1989&ndash;1998; expected roster 25 to 35 countries; panel 1985&ndash;2023</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Dividend window</td><td>Years 0 to 7 after transition; the decline's size predicts the 2010&ndash;2022 change in the Liberal Democracy Index</td></tr>\n                <tr><td>Welfare windows</td><td>Primary: earliest available three-year window within years 0 to 8; Power for interaction tests is low in samples of this size, and the clustered\n          standard errors rest on a modest number of clusters. The pre-committed MDES analysis defines what the\n          design can detect before estimation; the study will not detect a weak gate, and the results paper will say\n          so if the confidence intervals cannot exclude one.</p>\n          <h3><span class=\"limno\">2.</span>The welfare measure is a proxy</h3>\n          <p>Public health and education spending as a share of GDP measures fiscal effort, not universality, not\n          quality, and not usage by the middle class. Two countries with identical spending shares can differ in\n          whether public hospitals serve the well-off or only the poor. The proxy bias is conservative: measurement\n          error in the gate variable attenuates the interaction and biases against confirmation.</p>\n          <h3><span class=\"limno\">3.</span>Identification of the gate</h3>\n          <p>The welfare measure is pre-determined relative to erosion onset, but it is not randomly assigned; the\n          first democratic decade is itself a period of democratic politics, and governments that consolidated well\n          also maintained services. The balancing regressions, legacy-instrument 2SLS, within-Eastern-Europe\n          estimate, placebo moderator and early-erosion exclusion each address a specific version of this threat, but\n          none eliminates a third factor, state capacity, geography or geopolitical alignment, that drives both\n          welfare maintenance and democratic resilience. EU accession was itself a welfare-building force, so the\n          gate and the accession channel are partially entangled by construction.</p>\n          <h3><span class=\"limno\">4.</span>Measurement of the outcome and the treatment</h3>\n          <p>The Liberal Democracy Index is expert-coded, and its inter-temporal comparability is contested. Gini\n          comparability is limited by differing underlying surveys and income concepts; PIP and WID harmonization\n          does not remove the issue. The threat to the sequencing tests is asymmetric: a misdated erosion onset could\n          manufacture the confirmation pattern for H2. The three-year sustained-decline coding rule, alternative\n          onset codings, and the requirement that the sequencing pattern differ across welfare arms address it, and a\n          pure measurement artifact would not produce that difference.</p>\n          <h3><span class=\"limno\">5.</span>The placebo subsample problem</h3>\n          <p>The sharpest contrast, H5, requires a full-sample placebo. The OECD SOCX measure exists only for OECD\n          members, so it runs as a secondary subsample with its coverage limitation quantified. If the ILO or IMF\n          full-sample transfer series proves unavailable on OWID for a substantial share of the roster, that finding\n          is itself a registered limitation, and the paper would say so.</p>\n        </section>\n\n      </main>\n\n      <footer>\n        <p class=\"cite\"><span class=\"title\">The Welfare Gate: Pre-Fisc Inequality, Universal Public Services, and\n        Democratic Resilience in Post-1990 Democratizers.</span> A pre-registered research design.
